vignette: Kiet's eyes would glaze over, his mind suddenly hijacked by the memories of that fateful night in the detention center. It was as if the event had imprinted itself on his brain like a scar, refusing to be scrubbed away. The memory felt alien, like it belonged to someone else - a dissociation that only added to Kiet's sense of disorientation. He would relive the terror, the pain, and the helplessness in vivid detail, like a film playing over and over on repeat. These memories were not just random recollections; they were often triggered by seemingly innocuous events. Talking about the future with his colleagues at the accounting firm would suddenly transport him back to that cell, where his captors had taunted him about his bleak prospects. Striking up a conversation with strangers at the grocery store or on public transportation would remind him of the countless interrogations he endured, never knowing who might befriend or betray him next. These triggers only reinforced Kiet's deeply ingrained fear: that harm could lurk around every corner, and you can never truly know who will hurt you. This fear had taken hold of his life, dictating how he interacted with others and even how he perceived himself. He was certain that the torture had left him permanently changed for the worse - a broken version of the man he once was. As Kiet struggled to make sense of his experiences, he couldn't help but wonder what others would have done in his shoes. Would they have found a way to escape or resist? The thought haunted him, fueling the notion that somehow, he was to blame for not having stopped the event from happening. This self-doubt only made it more difficult for Kiet to piece together the events of that night - the memories remained jumbled and out of sequence, like a puzzle with missing pieces. The weight of these negative appraisals bore down on Kiet's memories, coloring how he recalled the traumatic event. His recollections were now tainted by his fear of harm, his sense of permanent damage, and his lingering self-doubt. These emotions swirled together in a toxic cycle, each reinforcing the others and making it increasingly difficult for Kiet to shake off the trauma. It had been years since the torture, but the memories still lingered, refusing to be silenced. The triggers continued to ambush him, dragging him back into that nightmarish world. Kiet's relationships suffered as a result - his divorce was, in part, a consequence of his inability to open up and connect with others. His work began to falter, too, as the flashbacks and anxiety made it harder for him to focus on even the most mundane tasks. One day, while reviewing financial reports at his desk, Kiet's mind began to wander back to that detention center. He felt himself getting lost in the memories once more, and something inside him snapped. He knew he needed help - not just to silence the memories but to untangle the web of negative thoughts that had taken hold of his life. With a mix of trepidation and hope, Kiet finally reached out for professional help, taking the first tentative steps towards reclaiming his life from the trauma that had haunted him for so long.
